deities: Kasbeswari Kali - a sandstone Mahishasurmardini (Dasabhuja Durga) idol worshipped as Goddess Kali; a Shivalinga sculpture at the feet of the idol on the same platform (unique Shakta-Vaishnava conjunction)
festivals: Annual Chaitra Mela (mid-April, Bengali New Year - 100,000+ pilgrims from India and Bangladesh, per earthtrip.in)

history.period: Late 15th century (built by Maharaja Dhanya Manikya, r. 1490-1520); temple completed/rebuilt 17th century
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: This temple is NOT in Kailashahar - the CSV town is WRONG. 'Kamala Sagar Temple' is the Kamalasagar Kali Temple (Kasba Kali Bari) at Kasba village, Bishalgarh subdivision, Sepahijala district, ~27-31 km south of Agartala, directly on the India-Bangladesh border; it is ~160 km from Kailashahar in a different district. Built on a hilltop by Maharaja Dhanya Manikya in the late 15th century (fort initiated by Maharaja Kalyan Manikya after defeating Surja of Bengal; the area was earlier called Kamalagarh/Koilagarh), the lake Kamalasagar was dug by Dhanya Manikya and named for his queen Kamala Devi. The deity is a 15th-century sandstone Mahishasurmardini (ten-handed Durga) worshipped as Kali because the base platform bears a Shiva image - the site conjoining Shakta and Vaishnava worship, with a Shivalinga at the idol's feet. Legend: Nawab Hossain Shah of Bengal attacked Kasba but was defeated by Dhanya Manikya's army. The temple terrace overlooks the border fence, Bangladesh's Kasba railway station and paddy fields; an annual Chaitra mela in April draws over 100,000 pilgrims. Documented with the corrected location. Coordinates (23.7403466, 91.15973) from the Tripura Tourism official Google Maps query for the Kasba Kali Temple.

name: Kamala Sagar Temple
town: Kasba (Kamalasagar), Bishalgarh (CSV town 'Kailashahar' is WRONG - temple is ~27 km south of Agartala on the Bangladesh border)
town_description: Kasba is a border village in Sepahijala district ~27-31 km south of Agartala, named from the Farsi 'kasba' (town). It centres on the 15th-century Kamalasagar lake and the hilltop Kasba Kali Bari, with the international border fence and Kasba railway station (Bangladesh) visible from the temple terrace; BSF presence is notable.
